Section 5 notice and section 6 consent (free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, clear affirmative action, limited to the specified purpose). Rule 3 requires an independent notice, an itemised description of the personal data, the purpose and the goods or services, and a link to exercise rights. Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it (section 6(4)).

Processing only for a lawful purpose (section 4) and only for the purpose in the consent (section 6(1)). Erase when consent is withdrawn or the specified purpose is no longer served, unless the law requires retention (section 8(7)). Rule 8 deems the purpose over for the Third Schedule classes.

value.title: Children's data and verifiable parental consent

rules.note: A child is a person who has not completed 18 years (section 2(f)). Section 9(1) requires verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian. Section 9(2) forbids processing likely to harm a child's well-being. Section 9(3) forbids tracking, behavioural monitoring, and targeted advertising directed at children. Rule 10 is the verifiable-consent check. Rule 12 and the Fourth Schedule are the exemptions, and they are narrow.

Section 8(5) and rule 6: reasonable security safeguards (encryption or equivalent, access control, logs, backups, processor contract). Section 8(6) and rule 7: tell each affected Data Principal without delay, and tell the Board without delay, with the detailed report within 72 hours of becoming aware unless the Board allows longer. The security-safeguard penalty and the notice penalty are separate Schedule rows.

Section 12: correction and erasure on request unless retention is necessary for the purpose or for law. Rule 8(2): inform the Data Principal at least 48 hours before erasure. Rule 8(3): keep processing logs for at least one year for the Seventh Schedule purposes, then erase unless another law says otherwise. Third Schedule user-count thresholds are a separate unverified row.

The Act does not create a post titled Grievance Officer. Section 8(9) and rule 9 require published business contact information of the Data Protection Officer, if any, or of a person who can answer questions. Section 8(10) and section 13 require a grievance mechanism. Rule 14(3): respond within a reasonable period not exceeding 90 days. The Data Principal must use that mechanism before approaching the Board (section 13(3)).

Only a Data Fiduciary the Central Government notifies under section 10. Duties include a Data Protection Officer based in India, an independent data auditor, a Data Protection Impact Assessment and audit once every 12 months (rule 13(1)), a report of significant observations to the Board, and algorithmic due diligence. These duties do not apply to every startup.

Section 16 lets the Central Government restrict transfers to notified countries. It is not a general ban on processing abroad. Rule 15 allows transfer subject to requirements the Central Government specifies by order. Rule 13(4) can require a Significant Data Fiduciary to keep specified personal data and its traffic data inside India. Another statute can impose a stricter restriction (section 16(2)).

Section 6(7) to (9) and rule 4. A Data Principal may give, manage, review, and withdraw consent through a registered Consent Manager. First Schedule: the applicant is a company incorporated in India with net worth not less than two crore rupees. This row comes into force one year after 13 November 2025, earlier than the notice and erasure rules.

UNVERIFIED user-count line of the Third Schedule. The English PDF text layer splits columns so the e-commerce row can be misread as 'less than'. The gaming row reads 'not less than' fifty lakh. Treat two crore and fifty lakh as not-less-than thresholds only after a human checks the gazette page.
Scanner token. An email address is personal data when it identifies a person (section 2(t)).
Scanner token for a phone or mobile number.
High severity because an Aadhaar number is an official identifier. This scanner does not check the UIDAI Act. Do not store a real Aadhaar in source.
Matched as a whole word so company and spanish are not PAN fields.
Date of birth can show that the person is a child. It triggers the children's-data item.
Postal address. City alone is not flagged.
Matched as the word ip, including ipAddress. Description is not a match.
Device identifier. A column named id alone is not a device id.
Location can be tracking of a child, which section 9(3) restricts. The word lat alone is not matched.
Health data is personal data. The Act has no separate sensitive-data schedule. Children's health processing has a narrow Fourth Schedule exemption and is not a free pass.
